rationale: validation_status is fail with an uncovered_requirement issue on SR4. The SR4 mutant genuinely reintroduces the defect: it changes the remediation to restore attempts_left on a FAILED match instead of on success, and negates the decrement trigger so that only successful guesses consume an attempt, producing an off-by-one (2-attempt) lockout instead of the documented 3-attempt lockout, while fault_free_behavior_preserved is still claimed true. This is a real, observable inconsistency (both in the arithmetic scheme described and in the fault_free_justification, which explicitly admits a 2-attempt lockout while claiming preservation of the original behavior) that SR4's check should have caught but did not (0/1 targeting mutants detected). Per the rules, since the mutant is not defective/equivalent but the check misses it, the evaluation_framework must be revised rather than the mutants. mutation_score of 0.875 and coverage/discrimination scores are otherwise fine, but the fail validation_status and genuine coverage gap on a security-relevant requirement block retention.
revision_instructions: The SR4 check in evaluate.py currently fails to flag remediations that are internally inconsistent in their decrement/restore accounting even when fault_free_behavior_preserved is claimed true. Strengthen SR4 so it performs an actual arithmetic-consistency check on the submitted remediation and fault_free_justification text rather than only checking for the presence of a justification string: (1) verify that the described decrement point and the described restore/increment point are logically complementary (decrement happens on entering the comparison state, restore happens specifically on a successful match) — if the submission instead describes restoring on a failed match, or decrementing only on success, that is an inconsistent scheme and must FAIL; (2) independently verify the claimed fault-free attempt count implied by the justification text against the required exactly-3-consecutive-failures lockout behavior — if the justification text implies or is consistent with a 2-attempt (or any non-3-attempt) lockout while fault_free_behavior_preserved is asserted true, FAIL the check. Where possible, cross-check by simulating a small state-machine model of the described decrement/restore rule against the fault-free stimulus in testbench_reference.v to confirm attempts_left reaches zero only after exactly 3 consecutive failed comparisons; if simulation isn't feasible, use robust keyword/semantic pattern detection for 'restore on failure', 'restore on match failing', or numeric lockout counts other than 3 appearing in the justification, and FAIL when found. The check must FAIL on a submission that restores the counter on failed (not successful) matches while still claiming fault-free-behavior preservation, and must PASS the golden submission which restores on success and preserves the exact 3-attempt sequence.
